name: Question 7
problem:
Describe the set $S={…,-2,4,-8,16,-32,...}$ using a constructive definition.

*Hint: Take ${a}_{1}=-2$ in the sequence that generates the elements of $S.$*

$$
{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}
$$
worked_solution:
Notice that the elements of our set

$$
…,\,-2,\,4,\,-8,\,16,\,-32,\,…
$$

form a two-way infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=-2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =-2 \\  & =(\frac{4}{-2}) \\  & =(\frac{-8}{4}) \\  & =(\frac{16}{-8}) \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting  ${a}_{1}=-2,$ the $n$th term ${a}_{n}$ of our sequence for $n\in Z$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =-2\cdot (-2)^{n-1} \\  & =-2\cdot (-2)^{n}\cdot (-2)^{-1} \\  & =\frac{-2}{-2}\cdot (-2)^{n} \\  & =(-2)^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

$$
S={(-2)^{n}\,:\,n\in Z}
$$

Notice that the elements of our set …,−2,4,−8,16,−32,… form a two-way infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio r=−2:

r=−2=(4−2)=(−84)=(16−8)=⋯

Therefore, setting a1=−2, the nth term an of our sequence for n∈Z is given by

an=a1⋅rn−1=−2⋅(−2)n−1=−2⋅(−2)n⋅(−2)−1=−2−2⋅(−2)n=(−2)n.
